note: Site-level monetization configuration. The Associates tag is supplied verbatim by the owner in the 2026-11-17 brief ('Selected Tracking ID:shopnow047c-20') — it is never invented, never modified, and validated here against the tagged format Amazon assigns (e.g. exampletag-20) and against the R-11 rule that an Associates ID must contain no Amazon mark. When this file carries no tag, every generator falls back to preview_link() and labels the links as non-earning. The tag changes only the href query string; the disclosure sentence (R-01), the link-level disclosure (R-02) and rel="sponsored nofollow" (R-17) are unchanged by it.
supplied_by: owner brief 2026-11-17 (recurring Zone2 brief, 'Selected Tracking ID:shopnow047c-20')
link_format: https://www.amazon.com/dp/{ASIN}?tag=shopnow047c-20 — Amazon's own help page gives the qualifying Special Link shape as http://www.amazon.com/dp/ASIN/ref=nosim?tag=YOURASSOCIATEID; the tag parameter identifies the Associates account the sale is tracked to (S24/S02 in ledger/sources.json)

rules_carried.R-01: Site-level disclosure sentence on every page, unchanged by tagging
rules_carried.R-02: Link-level disclosure '(paid link)' adjacent to every product link, unchanged by tagging
rules_carried.R-07: Every product link to Amazon carries the tag as a URL parameter (Special Link), and the observed evidence URLs recorded in ledgers are never rewritten to carry it
rules_carried.R-08: No sub-tag or per-visitor parameter is ever appended (Participation Requirements forbid associating a sub-tag or Associates reporting with a specific end user)
rules_carried.R-11: The tag contains no Amazon mark (checked at build time by tools/validate_data.py check_marks)
rules_carried.R-14: No competing-network attribution parameter is ever added to the same link
rules_carried.R-17: rel="sponsored nofollow" is emitted whether the link is tagged or a preview
